primitives.name: Pairwise Cost Regularization
primitives.verbatim_quote: To cope with such situations, we propose to add pairwise costs to the min-cost network flow framework.
primitives.assumptions: Pairwise interactions between object tracks are modeled via quadratic cost terms.
primitives.breakdown_regime: Quadratic terms introduce NP-hardness; requires convex relaxation for tractability.

layer2.mapping: Pairwise regularization acts as a kernel in the optimization space, encouraging or discouraging joint selections of object tracks.
layer2.telemetry: Suboptimality gap measured via rounding heuristic performance on relaxed solution.

primitives.name: Convex Relaxation and Rounding
primitives.verbatim_quote: While integer solutions to such a problem become NP-hard, we design a convex relaxation solution with an efficient rounding heuristic which empirically gives certificates of small suboptimality.
primitives.assumptions: Integer solutions are approximated using linear programming relaxation followed by rounding.
primitives.breakdown_regime: Rounding may fail under high overlap or ambiguous detection scenarios.

layer2.mapping: The rounding procedure provides a probabilistic certificate of solution quality, bridging continuous and discrete optimization domains.
layer2.telemetry: Empirical suboptimality bound computed post-rounding against ground-truth trajectories.

reasoning_traces.think:
The core insight of the work lies in extending classical min-cost network flow formulations to incorporate pairwise interaction terms between object tracks. These terms are modeled as quadratic penalties in an integer quadratic program (IQP), which is inherently NP-hard. To circumvent this, the authors introduce a convex relaxation—linearizing the quadratic cost—to allow efficient optimization via standard linear solvers. Subsequently, a Frank-Wolfe-style rounding heuristic is applied to recover integer solutions. This process introduces a trade-off between computational tractability and solution quality, but empirical validation ensures small suboptimality gaps. The method's strength resides in its generality: it supports arbitrary pairwise cost structures without altering the underlying optimization framework. The failure mode arises when detection accuracy is low due to occlusion or clutter, leading to poor initialization of the network flow graph. In such cases, the pairwise costs cannot sufficiently correct for erroneous associations unless they are specifically designed to penalize conflicting hypotheses.
